clue.text: Antimony pollutes dirty harbour

indicators.note: something that pollutes gets into the thing it fouls, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: dirty means grimy
Sb is the chemical symbol for antimony

explanation.surface: A grubby port being contaminated with a toxic metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Grimsby is a fishing port on the Humber estuary in England, so it names a harbour town.

clue.text: Grasp what's behind porkies, we are told

indicators.note: what we are told is heard rather than read, so the letters entered match a spoken phrase

parts.note: what's behind you is your rear; porkies is British rhyming slang (pork pies = lies) for lies

explanation.surface: Someone sees through the fibs they have been hearing.
explanation.walkthrough: PORKIES comes from rhyming slang: pork pies = lies. REAR LIES said aloud matches the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To grasp something is to understand it, which is to realise it.

clue.text: Very keen to keep working for unity

indicators.note: one word keeping another holds it within itself

parts.note: mad about something means very keen on it
a machine that is on is working

explanation.surface: An enthusiast eager to stay busy for the sake of harmony.
explanation.definitionFit: In philosophy and mathematics a monad is a single indivisible unit, so it stands for unity or oneness.

clue.text: Where one may read in no man's land?

definitions.text: Where one may read in no man's land?

parts.words: Where one may read in no man's land?
parts.note: no man's land in the First World War lay ... the opposing trench lines

explanation.walkthrough: Two senses together: spotting the implied meaning in a text, and the ground between two front lines.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for finding implied meaning, and literally the strip between two armies' trench positions.

clue.text: Poorly assembled program in divine setting

indicators.note: one piece sits in another
a setting holds a jewel around it, so one word surrounds the other

parts.note: to divine the future is to scry it
an app is a computer program

explanation.surface: A shoddily put-together broadcast set in a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'divine' looks like an adjective about the setting but is the verb meaning to foretell.
explanation.definitionFit: Something scrappy is made of bits and pieces, poorly put together.

clue.text: Chapter to be spoken or to be sung

parts.note: something oral is spoken rather than written

explanation.surface: A section of a work that may be either recited or performed in song.
explanation.definitionFit: Choral music is written for a choir, that is, meant to be sung.

clue.text: In brief panic attend to joint — I'm ready to carve

indicators.note: one piece placed in another
brief means cut short, so the last letter goes

parts.note: panic means alarm
to baste a joint of meat is to attend to it with its fat while roasting

explanation.surface: A cook in a hurry tends the roast, knife at the ready.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brief' drops the last letter of the panic word. The definition speaks as the answer: a stone ready for the sculptor's knife.
explanation.definitionFit: Alabaster is a soft fine-grained stone prized by sculptors for carving.

clue.text: Researcher coopts daughter for experiment

indicators.note: to experiment is to try things out in different arrangements, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A scientist recruits their daughter as a test subject.
explanation.definitionFit: A postdoc is a researcher who has finished a doctorate and works on a temporary research post.

clue.text: Bum getting smaller? Mine is hell

parts.note: bum is British slang for bottom
getting smaller means becoming less
a pit is a coal mine

explanation.surface: Someone dieting finds the struggle to slim their backside a torment.
explanation.definitionFit: The bottomless pit is a biblical name for the abyss of hell.

clue.text: Without exception one's abandoned building

indicators.note: something abandoned has been left behind, so these letters are dropped

parts.note: bar none means without exception

explanation.surface: Every single one of them has been left derelict.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one's' reads as 'one is': the word one is taken out of BAR NONE.
explanation.definitionFit: A barn is a farm building for storing crops or housing animals.

clue.text: Left back to dwell on the ball? It's up in the air

indicators.note: in an across answer, one piece on another comes after it
back means going in reverse, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship
O is a ball by its round shape
to dwell is to pause or linger

explanation.surface: A defender in football is told to hold the ball rather than rush.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left back' reads as a football position, but 'back' turns the word for left round.
explanation.definitionFit: The tropopause is the boundary layer in the atmosphere between troposphere and stratosphere, high above us.

clue.text: Tolkien's art?

parts.note: the three letters of art are the ... of the word ..., so the clue word is what the answer describes

explanation.surface: A question about the craft of the author of The Lord of the Rings.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as an instruction: the middle of EARTH is ART.
explanation.definitionFit: Middle-earth is the world Tolkien created for his fantasy novels, so it is his invention.

clue.text: Leaves here to instruct parent heartlessly

indicators.note: without a heart, so the central letters of the combined words are removed

parts.note: to instruct is to teach
daddy is an affectionate word for a father, a parent

explanation.surface: Someone advised to coach their father in a cold, unfeeling way.
explanation.walkthrough: TEACH + DADDY has ten letters; dropping the two middle ones, H and D, leaves TEACADDY. 'Leaves' are tea leaves, not departures.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea caddy is a small container for storing loose tea leaves.

clue.text: I keep time, but I'm missing from relaunch of 28 27

indicators.note: missing means these letters are lacking from the larger pool
relaunching something starts it again in a new form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the answers to 28 and 27 across together make the Latin phrase meaning remember you must die

explanation.surface: A clock-like device complains about being left out of a revived project.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the letters of the two linked answers, remove I and M, and rearrange the rest. The definition speaks as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A metronome ticks at a set rate to help musicians keep steady time.

clue.text: Having run with the others, I grabbed some food to get back

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run
et al is Latin shorthand for and others
to grab some food is to eat, here past tense ate

explanation.surface: After a group jog, someone snatched a snack to recover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get back' looks like recovering, but means getting even.
explanation.definitionFit: To retaliate is to strike back in return, getting back at someone.

clue.text: See 24
See 12
Perform greeting, welcoming non-female boss

indicators.note: welcoming someone takes them in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: ave is a Latin greeting, hail

indicators.note: F stands for female, and non- removes that letter

parts.note: a chief is a boss

explanation.surface: An office scene: a salute offered to a manager who is male.
explanation.definitionFit: To achieve is to accomplish or carry out successfully, a sense of perform.

clue.text: Airplane, a presidential one?

parts.note: ... Airplane was a 1960s rock band; Thomas ... was the third US president, so the band's name sounds like a president's plane

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests Air Force One; the word wanted completes the band name and is also a president's surname.
explanation.definitionFit: The word that precedes Airplane in the band's name, and the surname of a US president.

clue.text: Pasta to satisfy one's hunger, while taking in the Guardian?

indicators.note: taking something in holds it inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: fill I: to fill one, with I as one, satisfies hunger
the newspaper speaking of itself says us

explanation.surface: A meal eaten while reading the morning paper.
explanation.walkthrough: US goes inside FILL I after the F. The question mark flags the paper referring to itself as us.
explanation.definitionFit: Fusilli is a spiral-shaped Italian pasta.

clue.text: Moronic sort of letter

indicators.note: sort here is a verb hidden as a noun: the letters are sorted into a new order

explanation.surface: A rather foolish kind of written message.
explanation.definitionFit: Omicron is the fifteenth letter of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Walking about 30cm requires no energy

indicators.note: requiring none of something means it is left out

parts.note: one foot is roughly thirty centimetres
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A short stroll is so brief it takes no effort.
explanation.definitionFit: Going on foot means walking rather than riding or driving.

clue.text: See 4
Very disappointed about the Spanish holiday, without a phone extension

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: to be sick about something is to be very disappointed
el is the Spanish for the

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the letter is removed

parts.note: a fiesta is a holiday or festival in Spain

explanation.surface: A traveller gutted that their Spanish trip lacks a phone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' drops the A of the holiday word; 'about' puts the Spanish article and that shortened word inside the word for disappointed.
explanation.definitionFit: A selfie stick is a pole that holds a smartphone further out, literally extending it.

clue.text: Gordon Bennett is executed rudely, a Brit

indicators.note: an executed person is beheaded, so the first letter goes

parts.note: Gordon Bennett! is a British exclamation of surprise, like blimey!

explanation.surface: A man named Gordon Bennett is put to death in a crude way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'executed' looks like the fate of a person; it means losing the head letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Limey is a derogatory American slang term for a British person, hence rudely.

clue.text: Alliance blocks programme of legislator

indicators.note: to block something is to sit in its way, so one piece goes in the middle of the other

parts.note: a serial is a broadcast programme in instalments
NATO is the North Atlantic military alliance

explanation.surface: A coalition obstructs a lawmaker's agenda.
explanation.walkthrough: 'programme' looks like a political agenda but is a TV serial.
explanation.definitionFit: Senatorial means relating to a senator, a member of a legislature.

clue.text: See 28
In endless remembrance, I bury all but the last skull among others

indicators.note: one piece placed in another
endless means without its final letter

parts.note: memory means remembrance

indicators.note: all but the last means dropping the final letter

parts.note: to entomb is to bury

explanation.surface: A mourner's dark meditation on burying a skull with other remains.
explanation.walkthrough: MEMOR + I takes in ENTOM: MEM-ENTOM-OR-I.
explanation.definitionFit: A memento mori is a reminder of death; a skull is the classic example among others such as hourglasses.

clue.text: Looking witheringly on apparently good fastening

parts.note: pi is short for pious, outwardly virtuous
tying something is fastening it

explanation.surface: A sneer at what seems a good way to secure something.
explanation.definitionFit: Pitying someone can mean regarding them with condescending sympathy, a withering look.
